value: Emily arrived in Brierley.
unit: After moving to Brierley from New Brunswick, Mr. Pettifer acquired a reputation for eccentricity, frugality, and unusual domestic habits. He initially feuded with neighbor Nell Harcourt over her Jersey cow repeatedly breaking into his oat field. After Nell accidentally sold his cow to a buyer, she visited his home with a pink-frosted nut cake as a peace offering, leading to a warm resolution and the beginning of a close friendship between them. Over time, Mr. Pettifer offered practical, unvarnished advice to Nell regarding her teaching plans and story writing. When a thunderstorm struck the area, lightning killed his beloved parrot Nutmeg, leaving him deeply saddened. His estranged wife Emily later arrived in Brierley after seeing a newspaper prank, resulting in their domestic reconciliation, a newly cleaned house, and his return to church attendance. He continued to take a keen interest in Nell's life and writing, ultimately being invited as one of her cherished guests to her wedding.

unit: Lorna grew up in Seven Gulls as the intelligent and cheerful daughter of Frank Ainslie. Her early life was shattered at age twelve when she witnessed her four-year-old brother Julian die in an accident, and at fourteen she discovered her father after he committed suicide. To prevent Abner Vane from foreclosing on her mother's mortgaged farm, she reluctantly married Rufus Vane. Following her mother's death and Rufus's departure on a voyage, Rufus vanished, only for Captain Saul to later return a brain-injured, amnesiac man identified as Rufus, whom Lorna faithfully cared for over eleven years. She befriended Nell Carrow, though her hidden grief and intense jealousy over Nell's domestic happiness caused intermittent friction before she fully opened her heart. Summer boarder Adrian Treleaven stayed at her house, inspiring mutual romantic feelings that Lorna felt bound to hide. When Hugh Carrow arranged for the amnesiac man to undergo trephining in Montreal, the surgery restored his memory, revealing he was actually Rufus's lookalike cousin Laurence Vane, while Rufus had died of yellow fever years prior. During his stay, Nell Carrow introduced him to Captain Saul Garrick, whose life stories and journal inspired Adrian to write a novel.
